name: 冲绳地域背景·东岛联合演习（虚构设施部署）
description: Fictional six-hour island exercise on a real Taiwan/Ryukyu regional basemap. All bases, ports, deployments, force sizes and alert conditions are invented game assumptions, not real sites or readiness. Blue has two carrier groups plus two independent surface groups on separate patrol sectors, eight nuclear submarines, six fictional shore air stations including Zhejiang/Shanghai sector support, 144 shore aircraft including30 H-6J naval bomber proxies, and six generic Rocket Force cruise batteries with192 rounds. Red has six distant nuclear submarines. These are authored exercise forces, not a real OOB or a calculated attack requirement. H-6K/N and ballistic missiles are not modeled. Red has two initially stationary carrier groups at fictional anchorages, three air stations, two port complexes and routine airborne patrols. Only Red active orders are locked until its own sensors observe a hostile missile or a hostile hit confirms attack; routine flight/sensors and system self-defence continue. At each Red air host, two AAM-capable aircraft are immediately ready; the rest finish an authored360-second initial preparation interval, not a real readiness estimate. Blue receives one initial targeting-quality snapshot of all moored ships and the named facilities, not continuous satellite truth. BeiDou is navigation/timing background, not an imaging sensor. Blue scores carrier damage (60 maximum) and installation damage (40); Red scores preserved value plus up to20 counterstrike points. Blue must earn at least30 carrier and20 infrastructure points and exceed Red at six hours; otherwise Red wins. Aircraft kills do not directly score. Air stations and ports use labelled generic RTS proxies; no detailed runway, harbor bathymetry, ballistic missiles, satellite orbits or real facility layouts are modeled. Submarines start at least80nm from hostile ships. Shore collision uses charted polygons only. Hot opening: 64 Blue aircraft (48 strike and16 escort) and64 missiles are already airborne, representing authored pre-game launches. Aircraft and missiles are deducted from the above inventories, and elapsed flight fuel/time are charged. These counts and positions are game author choices, not a reconstruction or an attack recommendation. Joint service groups expose friendly task ownership for shore cruise batteries, shore aviation and naval forces. Their control shares ammunition accounting, replacement reserves and observed-feedback reviews. It is a fictional game exercise, not a model of actual Okinawa facilities or a real joint-strike plan. The opening is authored; later launches and combat remain ordinary engine actions. No extra detection/damage bonus or automatic force replenishment.
